summary: Phase 2 of suite deployment mode: myseliasan gains a node-owner registry and instance-to-instance command forwarding, closing the first of Phase 1's two documented multi-instance gaps and half of the operator-facing pain of the second. A node dials in and holds its control channel open to exactly one instance, so every instance previously knew only its own nodes -- the heartbeat reconciler fell back to an mTLS probe for nodes attached elsewhere and, where that probe could not reach them, falsely marked healthy nodes `lost`; opening a node's own screens (Settings dialog, recording playback) only worked when the browser request happened to land on the owning instance, a 1-in-N coin flip. New `apps/myseliasan/services/node_owner.go` (`NodeOwnerRegistry`) publishes a TTL-leased `nodeowner:<nodeId>` claim to the shared cache on connect (last-writer-wins, since a reconnect elsewhere is genuinely a new owner) and withdraws it on disconnect (new `ControlServer.SetOnDisconnect` hook, fired after the connection is torn down); `registry.SetControlPresence` now consults this registry's `ConnectedAnywhere` instead of the local connection map, fixing the false-`lost` heartbeat bug. New `apps/myseliasan/services/node_peer.go` adds the forwarding hop: a peer credential derived from `jwt.secret` via HKDF-SHA256 (domain-separated from the at-rest boot-log fingerprint so neither can be produced from the other -- no new secret to configure or leak), a `ForwardingSender` that decorates the existing narrow `ControlSender` interface so both the node command proxy and recording-stream playback become cluster-aware without either learning that instances exist, and `POST /api/internal/cluster/node-forward` (mounted outside session auth; only exists when clustering is configured) as the receiving side. New `cluster` config block (`infra/config/config_models.go`'s `ClusterConfigModel`: `advertiseUrl`, `ownershipTtlSeconds` default 30, `forwardTimeoutSeconds` default 30, `insecureSkipVerify`) controls all of this. Live-verified on two instances sharing one Postgres + one Redis with a real adopted mypintusan node: forwarding proven end-to-end (non-owning instance returned the node's real reply, HTTP 200; owning instance never forwarded its own traffic), and the false-lost fix proven with a control experiment (node's mTLS port pointed at a dead port so only the registry could report presence -- node stayed online across 3 heartbeat sweeps with zero false alerts; suppressing the registry claim past the grace window reproduced the `lost` bug on demand, and restoring the claim recovered it).
compatibility: An empty `cluster.advertiseUrl` (the default, and the value for every existing config.json) disables forwarding entirely: the node-owner registry degenerates to a local-only in-process map, `SetControlPresence` behaves exactly as it did in Phase 1 (and before), and no new listener or route is registered -- single-instance behavior is completely unchanged. The `POST /api/internal/cluster/node-forward` peer endpoint only exists on an instance when `cluster.advertiseUrl` is set there; it is never registered on a standalone or Phase-1-only install. Enabling clustering requires setting `cluster.advertiseUrl` to each instance's own directly reachable address (never the load balancer's) on every instance in the deployment; all instances must share the same `jwt.secret` (already required for Phase 1 clustering) since the peer credential is derived from it. Still NOT supported on a clustered deployment: live camera video across instances (WebRTC negotiates per viewer with media flowing outside the load balancer -- a node's camera stream is unreachable from an instance that isn't holding its control channel), fleet-rule correlation across instances (needs a shared event bus, planned Phase 3), the live SSE notification feed (still per-instance), and the Settings editor (still writes and restarts only the instance being talked to).
